s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin lesion with localized hair loss on the scalp and forehead
salient_findings: Arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the left side of the forehead, frontal scalp, and vertex area
Localized linear hair loss and hair thinning on the left scalp area
Presence of short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation on dermoscopic examination
key_facts: The patient is a man in his 50s
The lesion began approximately 10 years earlier
The patient received 2 doses of intralesional steroid via injection on a small bald patch on the vertex
The lesion gradually progressed to the frontal scalp and eventually made a linear furrow on the left side of the forehead
The patient denied any trauma history
The patient had no history of connective tissue disease
No evidence of systemic involvement, such as arthralgia, photosensitivity, or skin rashes
Dermoscopic examination revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation
The result of a hair pull test was negative
Histopathologic examination showed predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis
Direct immunofluorescence was positive with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels

shortlist.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive direct immunofluorescence and granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in dermal blood vessels

shortlist.label: Lichen planopilaris
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin lesion with localized hair loss and histopathologic findings of lymphocytic infiltrates

shortlist.label: Frontal fibrosing alopecia
shortlist.why_kept: Pattern of hair loss and presence of yellow dots and honeycomb hyperpigmentation on dermoscopic examination

shortlist.label: Scleroderma en coup de sabre
shortlist.why_kept: Linear, depressed skin lesion on the forehead and scalp, consistent with this condition's characteristic presentation

shortlist.label: Pseudopelade of Brocq
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of asymptomatic, progressive, and scarring hair loss, consistent with this condition

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of an asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the left side of his forehead, frontal scalp, and vertex area, along with localized linear hair loss and hair thinning, is consistent with Scleroderma en coup de sabre. The histopathologic examination showing lymphocytic infiltrates and lobular panniculitis, as well as the positive direct immunofluorescence, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient had no history of connective tissue disease and no evidence of systemic involvement, making this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Lichen planopilaris
rejected.why: The presence of lymphocytic infiltrates and lobular panniculitis is not typical of lichen planopilaris

rejected.label: Frontal fibrosing alopecia
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and histopathologic findings do not match the typical pattern of frontal fibrosing alopecia

rejected.label: Pseudopelade of Brocq
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and histopathologic findings are more consistent with an inflammatory process, rather than the non-inflammatory process seen in pseudopelade of Brocq
